'''Susan Ruth Wilson''' (19 March 1948{{r|eoas}} – 16 March 2020){{r|smh}} was an Australian statistician, known for her research in [[biostatistics]] and [[statistical genetics]], and for her work on the understanding of [[AIDS]] in Australia.<ref group=pub>{{citation|last1=Solomon|first1=P.J.|last2=Wilson|first2=S.R.|last3=Swanson|first3=C.E.|last4=Cooper|first4=D.A.|date=1990|title=Effect of zidovudine on survival of patients with AIDS in Australia|journal=Medical Journal of Australia|language=en|volume=153|issue=5|pages=254–257|doi=10.5694/j.1326-5377.1990.tb136895.x|pmid=2392071|s2cid=20749782|issn=0025-729X}}</ref><ref group=pub>{{citation|last1=Solomon|first1=P.J.|last2=Wilson|first2=S.R.|last3=Swanson|first3=C.E.|last4=Cooper|first4=D.A.|date=1990|title=Predicting the course of AIDS in Australia|journal=Medical Journal of Australia|language=en|volume=153|issue=7|pages=386–394|doi=10.5694/j.1326-5377.1990.tb125495.x|pmid=2215308|s2cid=25278359|issn=0025-729X}}</ref><ref group=pub name=back>{{citation|author1=Solomon, P.J.|author2=Wilson, S.R.|title=(Backcalculation of HIV Infection Rates): Comment|journal= Statistical Science| volume= 8|issue=2|date= 1993|pages=112–114|doi=10.1214/ss/1177011000|jstor=2246146|doi-access=free}}</ref> She edited the bulletin of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] from 1993 to 1998, and was president of the [[International Biometric Society]] from 1998 to 1999.{{r|ibsnom}}

==Education and career==
Wilson was born in [[Sydney]].{{r|eoas}}
She earned her Ph.D. in 1972 from [[Australian National University]];
her dissertation, supervised by [[P. A. P. Moran]], was ''Some Statistical Results in Genetics''.{{r|mgp}} She became a lecturer at the [[University of Sheffield]], but in 1974 returned to Australia to take a position as research fellow at the Australian National University. She became a fellow there in 1976, and a senior fellow in 1984.
In 1994, she was given a professorship in Statistical Science in the Centre for Mathematics and its Applications.{{r|eoas}} At her death, she was a professor emeritus of bioinformation science and statistical science at Australian National University{{r|anu}} and also  an honorary professor in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of New South Wales]].{{r|unsw}}

==Recognition==
She was elected as a member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 1979, as a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1991, as a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]],{{r|ibsnom}} and as an honorary life member of the [[International Biometric Society]] in 2012.{{r|lmibs}}
